hero.lead: Learn what you can do, how data freshness works, and where to find settings or legal info.
hero.freshnessBody: Data is refreshed regularly. You will see the exact scan time directly inside top lists and profiles.

dataFreshness.title: How up to date is the data?
dataFreshness.body:
SFDataHub relies on community scans. Some servers (for example many EU servers) are scanned roughly once per month by us and a few helpers – depending on our free time. Other servers (for example fusion servers) are scanned by other community projects and may have longer gaps between scans.

This means there can be several weeks or even months between two scans. You can always see the exact data age from the "Last scan: …" hint in top lists and profiles.

If you want your own profile to be more up to date, you can link your SFDataHub account and upload your own scans. That way you keep your profile fresh and help the overall database stay more current for the whole community.

what-is.question: What is SFDataHub?
what-is.answer: SFDataHub is a community project for Shakes & Fidget. It brings together scan data, player and guild profiles, rankings, guides and tools. It is not officially connected to Playa Games.

features.question: What can I do on SFDataHub?
features.answer: Use the DataHub to explore rankings, open profiles, compare scan data and track guild fights. The Guide Hub contains guides and calculators. The DataHub dashboard is the starting point for its available features.

account-needed.question: Do I need an account for the DataHub?
account-needed.answer: No. The DataHub and its released features are public. Scan management, SFtools imports and public settings work without signing in. Signing in adds account features such as synchronising account favourites.

local-pool.question: What is the local scan pool?
local-pool.answer: The scan pool contains full scans stored in this browser. Profiles, history and comparisons use the available matching data. You can add scans from the Scan Archive or import an SFtools file; these are two ways into the same local pool.

missing-data.question: Why are data or comparison values missing?
missing-data.answer: A profile or comparison needs suitable scans for that player, guild and period. Archive search can already find entries before the full raw scans are stored locally, so an empty pool does not rule out search results. Use the instructions below to add missing scans; identity comparisons may also require pre-fusion data.

browser-storage.question: Are my saved scans available on other devices or browsers?
browser-storage.answer: The scan pool belongs to this browser and its local storage. Another browser or device does not automatically receive it. Load or import the needed scans there separately. Clearing site data can remove local scans; account favourite synchronisation does not transfer the scan pool.

load-archive.question: How do I load archive scans into my pool?
load-archive.answer: Open Scan management → Scan Archive. Choose the relevant archive period and server, then load the required scans or group into the local pool. Wait for completion and check any errors. This saves data locally; it does not confirm identities or start an Identity Matching analysis.

archive-vs-import.question: How do archive scans differ from SFtools imports?
archive-vs-import.answer: Archive scans come from SFDataHub's shared scan archive. SFtools imports come from files you select on your device, whether created by you or received from someone else. Both can supply the local pool; the import source does not prove ownership of a player or file.

import-file.question: How do I import an SFtools file?
import-file.answer: Open Scan management and choose Import. Select your own or a received SFtools JSON file, check the preview and confirm the import. Wait until processing finishes and review any errors. The data is stored in this browser's scan pool.

publish-import.question: Are imported scans published automatically?
publish-import.answer: No. Importing a file adds it to the local scan pool. It does not automatically publish that file in the shared archive, and it does not prove that you own the player or the file.

data-age.question: How up to date is the displayed data?
data-age.answer: Freshness refers to the scan time of the actual observation, not when a file was imported or uploaded. Check the scan timestamp shown with the profile or result. Archive coverage and scan intervals vary by server; there is no guaranteed update schedule.

different-values.question: Why do the values differ from my current game state?
different-values.answer: A scan is a snapshot from its recorded time. Later levels, equipment changes or guild changes are not part of that snapshot. Check the scan time and selected comparison, and add a newer suitable scan if one is available.

find-tools.question: Where do I find each feature?
find-tools.answer: The DataHub dashboard links to Toplists, player and guild overviews, Fight Tracking, Scan management and Identity Matching. Player and guild search is available from the dashboard and the corresponding overviews. Features marked as under construction may have restricted access.

scan-counts.question: What do the scan numbers mean?
scan-counts.answer: The dashboard information button shows available archive file versions, archive scans verified as ready locally and SFtools imports in this browser. An import may also match an archive version, so these numbers must not be added together. Status and coverage hints explain partial or unverified counts; imports do not establish ownership.

select-servers.question: How do I select servers?
select-servers.answer: Open Toplists and use the server selection to choose the servers you want to include. The list is based on the available data for that selection. If the required scan data is missing, use the central archive instructions below.

filters-views.question: How do filters and custom views work?
filters-views.answer: Use the Toplist controls to filter the current list. Under Settings → DataHub → Toplists you can configure your player and guild views, including columns, their order and widths. Save your settings to keep the changes. These public settings do not require an account.

find-entity.question: How do I find a specific player or guild?
find-entity.answer: Use search in the DataHub or the relevant overview and select the player or guild result. Name and identifier searches help distinguish entries with similar names. Archive indexes can return results before full scans are local; detailed data and comparisons still depend on suitable scans.

player-views.question: What do the five player views show?
player-views.answer: General shows profile information; Progress focuses on progression; Base and Total show the corresponding attribute views; Fortress shows fortress information. The available fields depend on the scan. Total is available only when the necessary total values exist.

comparison-scan.question: How does the comparison scan work?
comparison-scan.answer: In the full player profile, use the comparison scan selector to choose an available historical observation. It sets the basis for the displayed differences from the current observation. If the required history is missing, add suitable scans using the central data instructions below.

compare-players.question: How do I compare up to three additional players?
compare-players.answer: Open the full player profile and use its player comparison search to add up to three other players. The selected players have separate colours and can be removed from the comparison. Matching data must be available; the current player and duplicate identities cannot be added again.

trend-compare.question: What is the difference between Trend and Compare?
trend-compare.answer: Trend follows the selected guild over time. Compare places selected guilds and metrics alongside one another using the available scan history. The chosen view and metrics determine what the chart can show; neither mode creates missing historical data.

guild-deltas.question: How does the comparison scan affect deltas?
guild-deltas.answer: The guild comparison scan sets the historical reference for differences from the current guild observation, including member comparisons where data is available. Changing this scan can change the deltas. It is separate from the chart period and does not change the recorded scan values.

chart-period.question: How do I change the chart period?
chart-period.answer: Use the guild chart's period control to choose the displayed range or a custom period. The chart shows available observations in that range. This does not select the comparison scan used for deltas; choose that separately.

identity-purpose.question: What is Identity Matching for?
identity-purpose.answer: Identity Matching helps connect player and guild references across server fusions. It lets you inspect candidates, status and confirmed mappings so that data can be related across old and new references. A name match alone is not a confirmed identity.

identity-scans.question: Which scans do I need for Identity Matching?
identity-scans.answer: You need suitable data from the predecessor servers before the fusion and the target server after it. Sparse or incomplete scans limit the comparison basis. Add the missing data using Scan management; downloading archive scans alone neither confirms identities nor starts analysis.

matching-status.question: What do matching status and coverage hints mean?
matching-status.answer: Status tells you whether a mapping is confirmed, unresolved or conflicting, or whether evidence is still missing. Coverage hints describe which relevant servers and periods are represented. Read them before analysing or confirming a mapping: thin coverage limits conclusions, and a suggested candidate is not automatic confirmation.

create-tracker.question: How do I create a guild for fight tracking?
create-tracker.answer: Open Fight Tracking from the DataHub and create a tracker for a guild. Use a guild from the available scans where possible, or create it manually. Review the member list and link or synchronise it with suitable guild scan data when needed.

record-fights.question: How do I record fights manually or from screenshots?
record-fights.answer: Open the guild tracker and use its fight entry function for manual data or its screenshot import. Check the recognised or entered opponent, date, result and member participation before saving. Screenshot recognition is a starting point and may need correction.

participation.question: What does the participation overview show?
participation.answer: It summarises the recorded participation of members in the fights stored in that tracker. Use it to review participation across the available fight records. It reflects what was recorded or corrected, not an automatic live feed from the game.

add-remove.question: How do I add or remove players and guilds?
add-remove.answer: Use the favourite action on a player profile or the guild selection to save an entry. To remove one, open the favourites menu or the corresponding overview, enter edit mode and remove the entry. Removing a favourite does not delete imported scans or a fight tracker.

guest-favorites.question: Can I use favourites without signing in?
guest-favorites.answer: Yes. Guest favourites can be stored in this browser and opened from the favourites menu or the relevant overview. They do not automatically appear on another device. Account favourites can be synchronised when you sign in.

edit-favorites.question: How do I edit my favourites?
edit-favorites.answer: Open the favourites menu or a player or guild overview and choose Edit favourites. Use the move and remove controls to change the list; guild entries also support dragging. Finish editing to return to the normal display.

context-actions.question: What does the right-click menu offer?
context-actions.answer: Right-click a favourite to open Profile or Toplist actions. Depending on the entry and context, you can open its profile, add a player to the comparison, focus it in Toplists, add its server or show only that server. Unavailable actions are disabled and do not change the selection.

favorites-devices.question: How do I use my favourites on other devices?
favorites-devices.answer: Sign in to the same SFDataHub account on each device to synchronise account favourites. Guest favourites are local to their browser. Synchronising favourites does not copy scans; load the required scan data separately on each device.

sign-in.question: How do I sign in?
sign-in.answer: Choose Log in and continue with Discord, then return to SFDataHub. After signing in, your account menu appears with your avatar and name. Public DataHub features remain usable without signing in.

account-benefits.question: What are the benefits of signing in?
account-benefits.answer: Signing in gives access to the account area and synchronised account favourites across devices. It does not automatically synchronise your local scan pool or prove ownership of a player. Public scan management, imports and settings remain available without an account.

identityAnchor.title: Anchored evidence
identityAnchor.description: A direct identity anchor. This is the strongest kind of positive signal, but it is still checked against contradictions and assignment conflicts.

strongSupport.title: Strong support
strongSupport.description: A reliable signal that strongly supports the candidate, especially when it is independent from other evidence.

support.title: Plausible support
support.description: A useful positive signal. It can support a match, but usually needs other evidence around it.

weakSupport.title: Weak support
weakSupport.description: Compatible evidence that is too thin, generic or low coverage to carry a match by itself.

neutral.title: Neutral context
neutral.description: Contextual information that does not meaningfully support or reject the candidate on its own.

warning.title: Warning
warning.description: A signal that reduces confidence or needs human attention, without always rejecting the candidate.

strongContradiction.title: Strong contradiction
strongContradiction.description: A serious conflict with the candidate. It usually blocks automatic matching unless other logic handles the case explicitly.

hardContradiction.title: Hard contradiction
hardContradiction.description: A blocker-level conflict such as incompatible origin, class or impossible progression.

rejected.title: Rejected candidate
rejected.description: The candidate conflicts with required identity constraints or was explicitly rejected.
rejected.effect: It is kept out of automatic linking.

weak.title: Weak candidate
weak.description: The candidate has only light or generic supporting evidence.
weak.effect: It can explain why the candidate appears, but normally remains review-only.

plausible.title: Plausible candidate
plausible.description: The candidate has a reasonable evidence pattern, but it is not strong enough for a hands-off decision.
plausible.effect: Useful for review, especially when combined with independent signals.

strong.title: Strong candidate
strong.description: Several meaningful signals point to the same historical identity.
strong.effect: Often enough for Ready if the candidate is not contested and coverage is sufficient.

anchored.title: Anchored candidate
anchored.description: The candidate has one or more high-value identity anchors.
anchored.effect: Can become Ready when contradictions, conflicts and coverage checks also pass.

originCompatibility.title: Origin compatibility
originCompatibility.description: Checks whether the historical and current player origin data can belong to the same identity.
originCompatibility.effect: Compatible origin is context. Origin mismatch is a hard contradiction.

classCompatibility.title: Class compatibility
classCompatibility.description: Compares the player class across historical and current observations.
classCompatibility.effect: Same class is context. Different class is usually a hard reject.

levelMonotonicity.title: Level monotonicity
levelMonotonicity.description: Checks that level does not move backwards across time.
levelMonotonicity.effect: A level drop is strong negative evidence.
levelMonotonicity.caution: Missing or sparse scans can make progression harder to judge, but they do not turn a regression into positive evidence.

levelProgression.title: Level progression
levelProgression.description: Judges whether the level gain between scans looks normal, plausible or extreme.
levelProgression.effect: Normal progression supports a match; extreme progression can contradict it.

baseMonotonicity.title: Base stat monotonicity
baseMonotonicity.description: Checks that base attributes do not decrease in impossible ways.
baseMonotonicity.effect: Stable or increasing stats fit continuity; regressions block or weaken a candidate.

baseUnchangedStats.title: Unchanged base stats
baseUnchangedStats.description: Several unchanged base stats create a strong fingerprint for the same player.
baseUnchangedStats.effect: This is strong support because exact stat stability is hard to reproduce accidentally.

baseSecondaryStability.title: Secondary base stability
baseSecondaryStability.description: Unchanged secondary base stats give another fingerprint-style continuity signal.
baseSecondaryStability.effect: This strengthens a player match when combined with other evidence.

baseOrdering.title: Base stat ordering
baseOrdering.description: The relative ordering of base stats stayed consistent.
baseOrdering.effect: Supports continuity, but is weaker than unchanged exact values.

fortressContinuity.title: Fortress continuity
fortressContinuity.effect: Continuity can strongly support a player match.
fortressContinuity.caution: A difference may simply be unavailable or non-decisive depending on the data.

petContinuity.title: Pet continuity
petContinuity.description: Compares pet-related progress as a light continuity signal.
petContinuity.effect: Helpful context, but generally weak by itself.

portraitContinuity.title: Portrait continuity
portraitContinuity.description: Compares the normalized player appearance from parsed portrait data.
portraitContinuity.effect: An exact match is usually weak support. It becomes normal support only when all relevant competing candidates have comparable portrait data and exactly one of them matches.
portraitContinuity.caution: Portraits are not percentage confidence, can be changed by players, and different players can share the same appearance. Race, gender, class, frame and horn color are not part of this comparison.

guildContinuity.title: Guild continuity
guildContinuity.description: Checks whether the player remains connected to the same resolved guild identity.
guildContinuity.effect: Supports player continuity, especially alongside direct player evidence.

exactName.title: Exact name
exactName.description: The normalized historical and current player names match exactly.
exactName.effect: A direct identity anchor, unless contradicted by required player properties.

fusionBaseName.title: Fusion base name
fusionBaseName.description: The current fusion name preserves the historical base name pattern.
fusionBaseName.effect: A strong direct identity anchor for migrated player names.

assignment.title: Assignment state
assignment.description: Shows whether this historical identity is already assigned elsewhere.
assignment.effect: Assignment conflicts prevent unsafe automatic linking.

exactName.title: Exact guild name
exactName.description: The normalized historical and current guild names match.
exactName.effect: Supports the candidate, but common names still need corroboration.

uniqueExactName.title: Unique exact guild name
uniqueExactName.description: The exact historical guild name points to a unique current candidate in the covered pool.
uniqueExactName.effect: Stronger than a plain exact name because ambiguity is lower.

fusionBaseName.title: Fusion base guild name
fusionBaseName.description: The current guild name preserves the historical base-name pattern after fusion.
fusionBaseName.effect: Strong support for continuity across the fusion.

sameCoa.title: Same CoA
sameCoa.description: The guild crest data stayed consistent between historical and current observations.
sameCoa.caution: CoA alone is not treated as proof of identity.

memberFlow.title: Member flow
memberFlow.description: Resolved member identities are compared between old and current guilds.
memberFlow.effect: High, mutual and dominant flow is one of the strongest guild continuity signals.
memberFlow.caution: Matched players count reliable identity matches, not the total roster size.

structuralRename.title: Structural rename
structuralRename.description: Member continuity indicates the guild persisted even though the name changed.
structuralRename.effect: Strong support because structure survives a rename.

leaderContinuity.title: Leader continuity
leaderContinuity.description: Compares the resolved leader identity when leader observations are available.
leaderContinuity.effect: Same resolved leader strongly supports continuity.
leaderContinuity.caution: Unavailable leader continuity is not proof against a match; a different resolved leader needs review.

officerContinuity.title: Officer continuity
officerContinuity.description: Compares resolved officer identities across old and current guilds.
officerContinuity.effect: One continued officer supports a match; multiple officers strengthen it.

leadershipCore.title: Leadership core
leadershipCore.description: Looks for a broader pattern of continued leadership identities.
leadershipCore.effect: Useful independent support for guild continuity.

guildProgression.title: Guild progression
guildProgression.description: Checks whether guild-level progression is compatible across the available scans.
guildProgression.effect: Usually a weak support signal because many guilds can progress similarly.

assignment.title: Assignment conflict
assignment.description: The historical guild identity is already claimed by another current identity.
assignment.effect: Prevents automatic linking and leaves the candidate for review.

reject.hardRejectEffect: This rejects the player candidate for automatic matching.

differentClass.title: Different class
differentClass.description: The historical and current player classes do not match.

levelDrop.title: Level drop
levelDrop.description: The current level is lower than a later historical observation would allow.

levelRegression.title: Level regression
levelRegression.description: The level sequence moves backwards across observations.

levelProgressionExtreme.title: Extreme level progression
levelProgressionExtreme.description: The observed level increase is too large for normal continuity.
levelProgressionExtreme.effect: This strongly contradicts the candidate and usually keeps it out of automatic linking.

originMismatch.title: Origin mismatch
originMismatch.description: The migration origin does not fit the historical identity.

baseAttributesContradiction.title: Base attributes contradiction
baseAttributesContradiction.description: Base attributes conflict with expected monotonic growth.

baseStatRegression.title: Base stat regression
baseStatRegression.description: A specific base stat regressed in a way that contradicts player continuity.

dashboardTrend.intervalDetails: Guild averages and growth per scan interval
dashboardTrend.metricHelp: Guild stand: average {{metric}} of contributing members. Bars show the absolute change between scans; points show change per day.
dashboardTrend.weightedHelp: The weighted trend adds the changes in adjacent valid intervals and divides them by their actual total duration. A falling line can still mean growth at a slower rate.
dashboardTrend.archiveSupplement: Supplementary monthly file: {{observed}}. Member basis from the complete observation at {{members}}; original observations and member timestamps are preserved.
dashboardTrend.archiveSupplementHelp: An explicitly verified monthly set may contain a complete guild source and files adding missing players or guild metadata. These additions do not create another guild observation when the complete source already establishes the member basis. Original observations stay separate; member values retain their actual timestamp.
dashboardTrend.excludedInterval: No interval value: at least one endpoint does not meet the chart coverage rule.

hatchingDescription.normal: The displayed end observation contains incomplete data for this metric.
hatchingDescription.faint: The displayed end observation is complete, but the interval starts with an incomplete observation. The interval evaluation is therefore limited.
hatchingDescription.none: Both the start and end observations are complete for this metric.

dashboardTrend.hatching: Partial values are shown only with a known total, an unambiguous member assignment, at least one valid contribution and at most five missing member contributions per metric at each endpoint. A complete end does not make an incomplete start complete retroactively. Hatching describes data coverage; the calculation is unchanged. The information area shows dates and valid/declared member counts for both endpoints. Member composition may differ. Focus or select an excluded date to inspect its observations.

excluded.unknown: Not shown: the total member count for this observation is unknown ({{used}} valid members).
excluded.empty: Not shown: no members have valid values ({{used}}/{{declared}}).
excluded.conflict: Not shown: conflicting member assignments for this observation.
excluded.excess: Not shown: the assigned or contributing member count exceeds the declared total ({{found}} assigned; {{used}}/{{declared}} valid).
excluded.missing: Not shown: more than five members lack valid values ({{used}}/{{declared}} valid).

dashboardCompare.selectMetrics: Please select at least one metric.
dashboardCompare.solid: Solid lines connect observed values, including partial averages. Progress, Base and Total also connect across missing scans with solid lines.
dashboardCompare.missingMarker: Hollow grey markers without a measured value indicate missing data. Their visual height is not a measured or estimated value; point details say “Not available at the time”.
dashboardCompare.partialMarker: All observed scan points have the same small size. On hover or keyboard focus, an equally sized hover circle with diagonal hatching in the guild colour marks an admitted partial average (at most five missing members).
dashboardCompare.partialLine: The value area shows captured and contributing members. Observations with an unknown total, conflicting membership or more than five missing metric values have no measurement point or hover target.
dashboardCompare.composition: Partial averages describe only the observed part of the guild. Changes can result from a different member composition.
